title: Candidate distinct covering system with minimum modulus 44 (Fable, 20 Oct 2026)
status: COVERAGE VERIFIED ON THE FINITE KERNEL; MODULUS DISTINCTNESS ARGUED STRUCTURALLY; CONDITIONAL ON OWENS' THESIS AND ON CODEX'S TRANSCRIPTION OF ITS SECTIONS 3.1-3.4
construction: 1. Owens' 42-system with TWO classes deleted: 10 (mod 42) (Section 3.4) and the class of modulus 43 in Section 3.14, i.e. the input of the top-level 43-arrow on the branch B = 2 mod 4 (hole 4) x 4 mod 5 (fourth input of the 5) x 2 mod 3 (middle input of the 3) that is filled with the set '1'. The inputs of that 43-arrow are ordered so that this is the class B x 1 (mod 43). All other moduli of Owens' construction are >= 44 (44, 45, 46, ... first appear at minimum modulus 45 and above). No other part of the construction borrows coverage from these two classes.

2. Hole H' from the first deletion: as in the M=43 certificate (product of all 7-adic states of 3 mod 7 with the explicit column set C'). Hole K from the second deletion: B x 1 (mod 43) minus what Sections 3.1-3.4 already cover; on the kernel the uncovered part of B is 7-inputs 1,2,3,6 entirely, input 5 only within 24 mod 25, input 4 nothing, input 7 (0 mod 7) recursively (70% of B).

4. 43 progressions, each covered by its own fresh-prime arrow (primes 89 and 97..317; 89 excludes 67 from its base primes). 31 of them cover H'; 12 cover K (they carry the condition x = 1 mod 43, which doubles the set count): k3, k6 = B x {3, 6} mod 7 (shape 2^2 3 5 7 43, primes 181, 191), k0 = B x 0 mod 7 (193), k1 = B x 1 mod 7 split mod 9 (271, 277, 281), k2 = B x 2 mod 7 split mod 16 (283, 293, 307, 311), k5 = B x 5 mod 7 x 24 mod 25 split mod 8 (313, 317). Every modulus produced contains its fresh prime, so all families are distinct from Owens' moduli, from the spares and from each other.
5. Finitize all arrows with auxiliary primes larger than 317.

verification.kernel: scratchpad m43/build44.py on plan14_44: Owens seed (minimum 43 transcription) + spares + 43 pieces cover every kernel state of H' and of the branch B (0 remaining of 50,803,200); the 43-condition is implicit since all K-pieces and K itself lie in 1 mod 43
verification.set_building: scratchpad m43/certify_orders2.py: 43/43 (shape, prime) pairs reach >= q-1 sets
verification.integer_sampling: scratchpad m43/mc_check2.py (t < 2^48 to avoid int64 overflow): 30,000 random x = 10 (mod 42): seed 29.5%, +spares 75.6%, +pieces 100%; 30,000 random x = 1334 (mod 2580) = CRT(2 mod 4, 2 mod 3, 4 mod 5, 1 mod 43): seed 29.8%, +spares 39.1%, +pieces 100%; 0 uncovered in both. Kernel-vs-integer semantics agree on 3,000 samples of each hole.
verification.modulus_distinctness: As for M=43: every fresh modulus contains its own prime (89 or 97..317); Owens' moduli contain no prime >= 97 and all his 89-moduli contain 67; spares are {2,3,5,7}-smooth exponent vectors absent from the transcription; inside each arrow Codex's exponent-range lemma applies (truncated machine tests with base primes <= 31 showed 0 duplicates for all shapes).

caveats: Inherits the unverified correctness of Owens' Sections 3.5-3.20 and Codex's transcription of 3.1-3.4 (audited by Fable for structure).

The identification of the modulus-43 class relies on Owens' text for Section 3.14 ('we start with the sets 1, 2, 4 and 8^ ... bringing us to the needed 42 sets'); the input order of that 43-arrow is chosen so that the set '1' occupies the class 1 mod 43.
